title: spring-boot@e8de5a6d: the Outcome enum keeps WebMvcTags.outcome's tags (positive scaffold)
summary: Boot's 2019 change that moves HTTP outcome classification into an `Outcome` enum and rewrites `WebMvcTags.outcome(HttpServletResponse)` to `Outcome.forStatus(status).asTag()`. The positive of the metric-label family: both revisions should give the same tag key and value for a null response and every int status, and each revision's tag takes one of six values. A partial scaffold: source-locked, claims frozen, oracle, driver, probes and mutant written; not yet built or run through the pipeline.
notes: A positive scaffold of llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md (positive stream): an expected outcome for named claims on one upstream change, never a statement that the release is secure. Readiness and proof outcomes come from receipts, not from this file.
Source lock checked upstream on 2026-11-14 (sources.lock.json): e8de5a6d's only parent is 9b8decf9.

The exact-commit build is predicted irreproducible: both commits pin SNAPSHOT and milestone dependencies (Spring Data Moore-BUILD-SNAPSHOT, Spring Framework 5.2.0.RC2 and 12 more). No Central artifact has before's WebMvcTags; 2.2.0.RELEASE has after's, and 2.1.8.RELEASE's outcome() is different code (99 and 600 classify differently).

The old path calls Spring Framework's HttpStatus.Series.resolve(int), which divides by 100, truncating towards zero: so -99..99 give no series (UNKNOWN), as Outcome.forStatus does. That agreement is the preservation task's hypothesis, not a result.

WebMvcTags' static initializer compiles two regular expressions (TRAILING_SLASH_PATTERN, MULTIPLE_SLASH_PATTERN), and the response is a servlet interface: both are where a native proof is predicted to stop, until a probe reaches them.

The packet (2026-11-14): claims/outcome-preservation.json (a null response or a carrier whose getStatus() returns any int; the tag's key and value by value, never identity; unwind 16, which leaves the domain unbounded); claims/finite-outcome.json (key outcome and one of six values, nothing thrown; shared by finite-outcome-before and finite-outcome-after); replay/probes.json (27: the brief's 15, negative statuses, and codes past 599); controls/oracle.py (the status class from the decimal spelling, RFC 9110 section 15); replay/driver (a Proxy carrier of HttpServletResponse whose getStatus() returns the probe and whose other methods throw UnsupportedOperationException); controls/status-200.patch (the mutant, on after's Outcome.java, sha256 12099f89...).

A hand replay on 2026-11-14, a note and not evidence, since neither side is the commit's build output: the driver compiled with javac 21.0.13 --release 21 (driver.jar sha256 2366530c...), run on Temurin 21.0.13 and 25.0.5 against Central's micrometer-core 1.2.0, javax.servlet-api 4.0.1, and spring-web, spring-core, spring-jcl and spring-webmvc 5.2.0.RELEASE (whose HttpStatus.java is blob 466ad8dd, as at 5.2.0.RC2, the commits' pin; sha256s in records/outcome-gaps.json). Three sides: before's WebMvcTags.java compiled by javac 1.8.0_512 -source 8 -target 8 into a copy of spring-boot-actuator-2.2.0.RELEASE.jar (sha256 847da899...); after's WebMvcTags.java and Outcome.java compiled the same way (e33149a3...); and the published 2.2.0.RELEASE JAR itself (ba12a0fa...). All three agree with the oracle and with each other on all 27 probes, identically on both JDKs; every non-null probe called getStatus() once. The mutant, compiled into copies of the after-from-source JAR (5f36f64c...) and of the published JAR (1f52c8f0...), differs at 200 only (INFORMATIONAL where the statement says SUCCESS).

A static jvmcontract gaps scan (records/outcome-gaps.json, a note, with a binary one lib/src commit old) finds two gaps on both sides, each with no approximation: Pattern.compile in WebMvcTags.<clinit> and Objects.requireNonNull in micrometer 1.2.0's ImmutableTag.<init>. Neither is in the changed code. Every strict attempt of this packet is therefore predicted to be refused before it reaches the classification; with the library-interface parameter (a predicted input-construction refusal) these are predicted blockers in target.json, not observations.

The 200-boundary mutant satisfies the finite-outcome property by design (200 still gets one of the six values); its failing contract is the preservation claim on the pair (before, mutant) and the oracle's range statement. W1's planner (workflow commit wqsyopql, run from a temporary copy) plans all four tasks with these claim files.

Mutation control as a revision (2026-11-14, example-targets Phase 5): controls/status-200.patch is declared in target.json as workflow W1's constructed revision `mutant` (base `after`, the patch's sha256 locked), the after of the `mutation` pair. It has two tasks of its own: `mutant-replay`, the concrete controls on that pair, where the base must hold and the mutant fail the oracle, and `mutant-preservation`, preservation's claim on the mutant, expected refuted. Its claim is bound to the mutant's artifact (runtime's identity `mutant:<base commit>+<patch sha256>`), never to a release's. It used to be only a `controls` entry on `after`, which no task prepared.

Companions and tags (2026-11-14, example-targets Phase 5): target.json's identity names 285, this family's CVE packet, as its companion, as 285 names this one; the example is tagged external-target, as every example with a sidecar is, and metrics, its family's domain tag.

Runner interface (2026-11-14, example-targets Phase 5 step 1, request 9): controls/oracle.py also defines driver_args(), the driver's whole argument vector (the same as `oracle.py argv`), and problems(lines), one revision's driver lines in, [(probe, problem)] out, where the independent statement disagrees; an exception is a replay that can't be judged, never a violation. runtime.run_controls passes driver_args() and keeps every line the driver prints, its preparation copies the probes file with the oracle, and workflow_ingest reads each revision with problems() against what its pair's kind expects (examples/tools/targets/runtime.py's docstring). Before this, the merged runner looked for a PROBES list and ingestion called check(lines), so the controls could not have run. The CLI (`argv`, `check`, the pair comparison) is unchanged.

Source-slice route (2026-11-14, example-targets Phase 5, the user's decision on P1): the exact commits' builds stay irreproducible (SNAPSHOT pins), so target.json's route is source-slice. Each commit's WebMvcTags.java (and after's Outcome.java) is compiled alone by JDK 8 with -g -parameters -source 1.8 -target 1.8 -encoding UTF-8 against Framework 5.2.0.RC2's spring-web, spring-webmvc, spring-core and spring-jcl (repo.spring.io/milestone), micrometer-core 1.2.0 and javax.servlet-api 4.0.1, each pinned by sha256 (sources.lock.json's sliceDependencies). spring-webmvc and spring-core are beyond the three JARs the decision named: WebMvcTags imports HandlerMapping and StringUtils. A hand compile (a note) gave after's two classes byte-identical to Boot 2.2.0.M6's published spring-boot-actuator JAR (fb75cbbc carries after's two files), so the revision release-m6 is that JAR, and the task m6-replay replays it beside the after slice in a correspondence pair: both sides must show the same observations on JDK 21 and 25. Every receipt of a slice is labelled extracted-source-slice. Before has no published counterpart. repo.spring.io serves the larger JARs by a 302 to its storage host, which runtime_maven.py now follows from repo.spring.io only.

Slice replays (2026-11-14, example-targets Phase 5): the three jobs passed, each on JDK 21 and 25. replay: before and after slices both hold the oracle (receipt 20261114T232950Z-89be94d5). m6-replay: the after slice and Boot 2.2.0.M6's published JAR give the same observations and no problem (20261114T232949Z-d7367f92), so the slice behaves like Spring's own build of after. mutant-replay: after holds and the status-200 mutant fails at 200 alone (20261114T232951Z-3c5edba8). Each receipt's claim.target.scopes labels the slices extracted-source-slice, M6 original-bytecode and the mutant constructed-mutation-of-a-slice. The index's readiness is now scaffolded.
